record.what_it_does: Creator/info-product checkout and payments platform (FanBasis, rebranded Commas) with REST API.
record.auth_notes: Each merchant has an API key, sent in an `x-api-key` header to https://www.fanbasis.com/public-api/. The base URL stayed the same after the rebrand to Commas. Keys reportedly carry granular scopes such as checkout-sessions, refunds and webhooks. No OAuth was found, so a multi-user toolkit would need each user to paste their own key. These details come from search-indexed text of commasdocs.com and a GitHub mirror of the same reference. The docs site is a JavaScript single-page app, so the page itself could not be rendered to confirm them.
record.access_notes: Signup is public through "Get started" at commas.com/login, and no application step is shown. The indexed docs say keys are created in the dashboard under Account → API Keys, or with the CLI (`commas keys add sandbox`). Sandbox keys are separate and come from sandbox.commas.net. Pricing is not published: each business gets an individual quote, with fees taken per transaction. Taking live payments probably requires merchant onboarding and KYC as a payment processor, but this was not confirmed. Confidence in self-serve developer access is low to medium.
record.api_breadth_notes: Indexed docs describe checkout sessions (create, get, delete, embedded), checkout transactions, refunds, subscription extension, products, discount codes and webhook subscriptions (list, create, delete, test). That is probably around 15–30 operations. The full list could not be counted because the docs SPA did not render.
record.mcp_notes: The vendor's own MCP server is in beta. The commas.com homepage lists "MCP (beta): Run Commas from your AI assistant", covering checkout links, refunds and reporting. Per the indexed commasdocs.com text, the remote URL is https://www.fanbasis.com/mcp and it authenticates with a FanBasis API key. A one-click Claude Desktop install also exists. Zapier separately lists a FanBasis MCP integration, which is third-party.
record.blocker_notes: The API key is per merchant, with no OAuth, so each user must supply their own key. The product was renamed: FanBasis became Commas on 2026-07-14, but the API host is still fanbasis.com. Pricing is quote-based, and live-payment onboarding is unverified. The docs site (commasdocs.com) is a JavaScript SPA that automated fetching could not render, so the endpoint details rest on indexed text.

evidence.quote: FanBasis did not shut down. It changed its name to Commas as part of a rebrand on July 14, 2026.
APIs and embeddable components, live in days not quarters.
Run Commas from your AI assistant.
No published pricing. You get a quote.
There are APIs and SDKs, and an MCP integration in beta for connecting AI assistants.

record.needs_human: commasdocs.com is a JavaScript SPA that WebFetch could not render; it only showed "Unpacking...". The auth header, scopes, sandbox host, endpoint list and MCP URL (https://www.fanbasis.com/mcp) are taken from search-indexed text of that site, not from a rendered page. A human should open commasdocs.com in a browser and confirm three things: the MCP URL, whether sandbox API keys are fully self-serve, and whether live keys require merchant underwriting.
